kpis.name: NUZOLVENCE
kpis.explanation: First-in-class medicine for the treatment of uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea
kpis.description: NUZOLVENCE received FDA approval in December 2025 for the treatment of urogenital gonorrhea in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older weighing at least 35 kg. Commercial launch is expected in the second half of 2026.

risks.title: Generic competition on key products
risks.summary: The arrival of competing generics for Advair, RELVAR/BREO and ANORO could drastically reduce royalty income.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in the first section of the 10-K, with strong language (materially affect, significantly lost). It directly concerns the two products generating the majority of revenues. The Competition category is highly weighted here.

risks.title: Dependence on GSK for commercialization
risks.summary: The company is entirely dependent on GSK for development, marketing and sales, with no influence over its decisions.
risks.score_rationale: Repeated multiple times with alarming language (materially affected, no control). Central position in the 10-K. Total operational dependence on a single partner constitutes an existential risk.

risks.title: Mandatory price negotiation by Medicare
risks.summary: RELVAR/BREO and ANORO will be subject to price caps imposed by Medicare starting in 2027, reducing revenues.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is new (Inflation Reduction Act 2022), with a predictable short-term impact (2027). Precise and concerning language: negotiated prices, reduction in net prices. Direct impact on future revenues.

risks.title: Pricing and reimbursement pressures
risks.summary: Pressure from insurers, governments and healthcare managers to reduce costs weighs on pricing and profitability.
risks.score_rationale: Frequently mentioned in the text (PBMs, cost management, market access). Repetitive and concerned language. Less existential than others but structural and persistent.

risks.title: Therapeutic paradigm shift
risks.summary: Evolving medical guidelines or standard-of-care treatments for asthma and COPD could marginalize key products.
risks.score_rationale: Discussed as a major risk related to evolving standards (e.g., GOLD). High potential impact on medical acceptance. Cautious but recurring language.

risks.title: Limited prescriber acceptance
risks.summary: Commercial success depends on acceptance by physicians, patients and payers, which is not guaranteed despite regulatory approval.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in launch-related risks (e.g., difficulties with PBMs in 2013). Language emphasizes uncertainty regarding medical adherence and reimbursement.

risks.title: Cyberattack or system failure
risks.summary: An information system failure or cyberattack could disrupt the company's critical operations.
risks.score_rationale: Brief but explicit mention (our operations could be disrupted). Secondary position in the document. Generic risk but present in a data-sensitive sector.

ai_positioning.summary: Innoviva invested in Beacon Biosignals, an AI-based neurotechnology company, by committing $17.5 million in a Series B round. The company does not report internal use of AI in its core operations.
evidence: $17.5 million investment in October 2025 in Beacon Biosignals, Inc., an AI-based neurotechnology company
